title: Kestrel and the Salt Revisited
premise: Sable Dravenmoor, the last swordspeaker, has hidden his oath for a decade in Salt Revisited, a port city built on the drowned ruins of the kingdom that outlawed magic. When prayers to the old gods start being answered — violently, indiscriminately — Sable's charms stop working as charms and start working as doors, dragging him into a war between the usurper's armies and the free cities. Hunted by an inquisitor who was once his sworn sister, he gathers a ragtag found family of smugglers, god-touched orphans, and a deserter priest, seeking the Doorway: the last gate out of Kestrel, a country that officially no longer exists. In the end Sable learns the Doorway opens only for someone willing to give up their name and oath — and he pays that price, becoming the door itself so his family can pass through free, while the gods, grateful, let him remain as a presence in the salt wind rather than a man.
about_author: Mara Kavanagh is a former maritime archivist who spent six years cataloguing salvaged letters from drowned coastal towns before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people who survive institutions meant to erase them.

chapters.title: Charms for the Godless
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. He sells a luck-knot to a dockworker's daughter and feels his magic answer something that isn't him — a prayer, answered from below the harbor. The emotional beat is quiet dread: ten years of hiding ending without his consent.

chapters.title: The Answering
chapters.summary: Multiple POV, anchored on smuggler captain Ives Rell. Across the city, answered prayers manifest as small miracles and one catastrophic tide. Sable's stall burns with cold fire; he saves three strangers and is seen doing it. Beat: exposure, and the first flicker of reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Ashen
chapters.summary: Ashen's POV. The usurper's inquisitor arrives in Salt Revisited — she is Wren, Sable's former oathsister, now wearing iron and a new name. She interrogates him gently, giving him a night's head start she shouldn't. Beat: grief disguised as duty.

chapters.title: The Deserter's Psalm
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Fleeing with Ives and the orphan Tam, he shelters with Brother Odo, a priest whose god has started answering him against his will. Odo reveals the Doorway legend: the last gate out of dead Kestrel. Beat: hope arriving as burden.

chapters.title: Salt Roads
chapters.summary: Ives's POV. The found family travels the flooded causeways toward the ruins of Dravenmoor Keep, dodging conscription sweeps. Tam begins hearing the gods too. Beat: bickering, campfire warmth — belonging forming under pressure.

chapters.title: What the Keep Remembers
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In the ruined keep, the walls replay the massacre that ended the oaths. Sable confronts why he alone survived and what his oath actually binds him to. Beat: shame transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Iron and Old Names
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She corners them at the keep; Odo dies holding the line, his god answering through him one final time. Wren lets Sable go again — and this time it costs her her rank. Beat: sacrifice, and the enemy revealed as family lost.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Burn Late
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The usurper's vanguard reaches the coast; refugee columns choke the salt roads. The group becomes accidental leaders of hundreds. Beat: the price of survival made collective — you can't save everyone, but you can carry some.

chapters.title: The Door in the Drowned Country
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. At the Doorway beneath the sunken capital, the gods offer terms: passage for those he loves, in exchange for his name and oath. Wren arrives not to arrest him but to take his place; he refuses her. Beat: climax — love outbidding guilt.

chapters.title: Kestrel and the Salt
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Sable speaks his last word as a named man and becomes the Door itself; his family passes into the free cities, carrying his memory. Epilogue: years later, a salt wind follows Tam like a blessing. Beat: mourning braided with peace — belonging survives the self.
